stability_estimation._comment_cs_window_floors: CS validity repair, FOURTH and FINAL pass (100 Hz time base + corrected floor derivation, 2026-09-02, thesis_notes.md 'PHASE 1: floor derivation, third pass' and the sign-off session's own clarification round). SUPERSEDES all three earlier attempts (kept in thesis_notes.md, not deleted -- including the SECOND attempt's own real-data FALSIFICATION and the THIRD attempt's own 0.2s hypothesis, ALSO since retested and rejected). History, briefly: attempt 1 bootstrapped a single window's own slope variance (no natural knee, wrong target). Attempt 2's phase-median bootstrap sampled the WHOLE moving population, landed on (n=10, span=0.01 rad) @ 50 Hz, passed its own 15% criterion, then FAILED catastrophically on real Phase 4 data. Attempt 3 restricted the bootstrap to cornering-only stretches, exposed the deeper lesson that bootstrap relative std measures reproducibility (precision) never closeness to the true tangent (accuracy), abandoned the bootstrap as the deciding criterion, and picked (min_window_s=0.2, span=0.02 rad) via DIRECT real-data Phase 4 validation against 5 candidates spanning 0.2-2.0s -- clean result, matched the pre-registration reasonably well. ATTEMPT 4 (sign-off clarification round, same day): user asked for the 0.1s (chair's own LITERAL, unmodified reference) comparison that attempt 3 never actually ran. Isolated duration-only bootstrap (span fixed at 0.02, cornering-only population) found n=10 (0.1s) and n=20 (0.2s) STATISTICALLY INDISTINGUISHABLE at every tested phase length, both axles (1-2pp differences, no consistent direction) -- the bootstrap never supported 2x. Direct real-data validation at (0.1s, 0.02rad) then found it reproduces the (0.2s, 0.02rad) result almost exactly across all 14 corners (identical negative-count 7/14 CSf, 2/14 CSr, same corners flagged) -- C4 rear even reads a STRONGER negative at 0.1s (-0.134 vs -0.042). CONCLUSION: no evidence (bootstrap or direct validation) supports the 2x deviation from the chair's own value. cs_min_window_s reverted to 0.1s -- the chair's LITERAL, completely unmodified reference -- once the real fix (the 100 Hz grid, PHASE 0) was in place. The 0.2s hypothesis is recorded as TESTED AND REJECTED, not merely superseded by a better number: it worked, just no better than the simpler, zero-deviation choice.
stability_estimation.cs_min_window_s_derived_from: diagnostics/inspect_cs_floor_candidate_validation.py + inspect_cs_duration_only_comparison.py, 2026-09-02 -- see _comment_cs_window_floors. Exactly the chair's own literal default (10 samples @ their 100 Hz = 0.1s), zero deviation, now that the real fix (PHASE 0's 100 Hz grid) supplies the sample count that default always assumed. A 0.2s hypothesis (double the chair's value, motivated by an a priori 'this car's alpha comes from an ESTIMATED beta -- kinematic or EKF/auto-fit, a noisier Level 1-3 chain -- vs the chair's own MEASURED beta channel, so more averaging seemed plausible') was TESTED AND REJECTED, not just superseded: an isolated duration-only bootstrap (span held at 0.02 rad, cornering-only population) found 0.1s and 0.2s statistically indistinguishable at every tested phase length, and direct real-data Phase 4 validation confirmed the two floors reproduce the SAME worst-lap population almost exactly (identical negative-corner counts, same corners flagged, C4 rear even reads a stronger negative at 0.1s). The plausible-sounding physical story was not supported by either form of evidence gathered -- recorded honestly rather than left implied.
stability_estimation.cs_min_window_samples_floor_derived_from: Absolute floor protecting a much slower log (e.g. this project's own GT3 Paul Ricard census found 20 Hz -- thesis_notes.md) from deriving too few samples for a meaningful 2-parameter OLS fit: 0.2s*20Hz=4 samples would round below a robust minimum; floored at 5 (same magnitude as cs_phase_min_valid_samples's own robustness reasoning), mirroring modules.longitudinal_stiffness's own min_samples_floor precedent (PLAN.md STEP 3, 50 Hz adaptation).
stability_estimation.cs_min_slip_angle_span_rad_derived_from: diagnostics/inspect_cs_floor_candidate_validation.py, 2026-09-02 -- see _comment_cs_window_floors. Rate-independent (alpha-domain, radians) -- no sample-rate correction applies. Reverted from attempt 2's falsified 0.01 rad back to 0.02 rad (the chair's own original span) after direct real-data validation; unaffected by the separate cs_min_window_s duration question (0.2s vs 0.1s) -- span was never the axis in question there.
stability_estimation._comment_cs_max_window_m: CS validity repair, locality cap (2026-09-02) -- measured under the (then-current) 0.2s/0.02rad floor, re-confirmed valid for the FINAL 0.1s/0.02rad floor: since SPAN (unchanged, 0.02 rad), not min_window, is what actually governs the natural window size in practice (real cornering data rarely satisfies 0.02 rad within either 10 or 20 samples -- both floors showed near-identical achieved-window distributions in every comparison run), this cap does not need re-deriving for the 0.1s/0.02rad final choice. diagnostics/inspect_cs_max_window_locality_sizing.py measured the NATURAL (uncapped) window's own metre extent restricted to real corner-bracket samples only (moving, non-kerb, inside an actual corner's own entry_1_brake-to-exit_5 span): median footprint front=24.1 m, rear=35.4 m (p90 82.7 m / 110.7 m -- both notably larger than the earlier falsified floor's own 9.1 m/11.1 m, since a bigger span requirement naturally needs more track distance to satisfy). Set at 1.5x the more demanding (rear) axle's own median -- 1.5*35.4=53.1, rounded to 53.0 m. Verified this does not silently truncate any of the 14 physical corners at EITHER floor (diagnostics/inspect_cs_floor_candidate_validation.py's own (0.1,0.02) and (0.2,0.02) runs: all 14 corners present in both axles' worst-lap populations both times) -- the earlier, now-superseded 17.0 m value would have been too tight for this span (a 0.6s/0.06rad candidate tested in an earlier run, at the OLD 17.0 m cap, zeroed out every single corner, confirming the cap must scale with whichever span it is paired with). LIMITATION, checked and recorded (thesis_notes.md): a corner-bracket LENGTH check confirms 53 m never approaches even the smallest physical corner (116.0 m, C7), but a corner-to-corner GAP check finds several real gaps smaller than 53 m (8.5-17.8 m, plus one 0.0 m pair) -- the cap does not guarantee a window never bridges into a neighbouring corner for those specific tightly-sequenced cases, though it did not visibly affect the Phase 4 result. Applied as a real TRACK DISTANCE via state['s_m'] inside the growth loop (reconstruct_cs_window_start/compute_cs_for_axle), not converted to a fixed sample count -- a corner's physical scale is a distance, not a duration, so the cap must not silently mean something different at a slow vs a fast corner. A window that cannot meet BOTH floors within this distance cap reports NaN (no signal) rather than accepting a non-local fit.
stability_estimation._comment_cs_phase_min_valid_samples: CS validity repair part A, Phase 2 (2026-09-02). Per-phase noise floor for summarise_corners's cs_ratio_f/cs_ratio_r stat blocks: a phase's median is reported as NaN (no signal, dropped from the Stage-2 min) when fewer than this many finite CS_ratio samples back it. Set at 5 -- the smallest sample count for which a median is not simply one of the phase's own most extreme readings (n=1: the median IS the single sample; n<=4: the median is an average of two extreme-adjacent points) -- a general backstop for any phase, not specific to apex_3 (whose own structural undersizing is separately addressed by apex_region below, replacing its CS reads outright rather than gating them).
stability_estimation._comment_stab_phase_no_braking_floor_bar: v3 diagnostics Part B2/C2 (2026-09-03, thesis_notes.md 'v3 diagnostics, Part B2' and 'Part C: stability-statistic phase-validity gating'). entry_1_brake's own stability_observed_Nm_per_deg stat gets the SAME cs_phase_min_valid_samples sample-count gate CS_ratio already has (reused, not re-derived -- that value's own justification, 'the smallest sample count for which a median is not simply one of the phase's own most extreme readings', is generic to any per-phase median statistic, not CS-specific), PLUS this second, brake-specific check: a phase whose max brake_f_bar never clears this floor had no real braking event at all, so its stability reading is reporting noise from an essentially-unloaded phase, not a real destabilising brake event. Value derived from GT3_PRC_MLA-v3's own log_pbrake_f distribution (diagnostics/inspect_v3_brake_phase_stability.py, run against a throttle>90% reference population -- unambiguously not braking): 32829 samples, mean=0.0049 bar, p99=0.0 bar, one single 6.03 bar transient (0.003% of the population, not sustained). Set at 3.0 bar -- comfortably above the population's own effective noise ceiling (p99 exactly 0) and below every real braking event found (entry_1_brake phases with genuine braking read 13.58 bar even for a light dab; general moving-sample braking events range to 88 bar), with margin against the single observed transient outlier.
stability_estimation.cs_linear_slip_threshold_rad_derived_fro: diagnostics/inspect_cs_window_floor_derivation.py, linear_region_end, 2026-09-02 (CS validity repair part A, Phase 1). Binned the session's own Fy-vs-alpha cloud (both axles, folded to a single sign via the tyre curve's expected odd symmetry, moving & non-kerb samples) with sliding 0.04-rad-wide windows (matched to the re-derived cs_min_slip_angle_span_rad, not an arbitrary narrow bin -- a narrower bin reproduces the same small-span sampling noise Phase 1's own N/span sweeps diagnosed) stepped by 0.005 rad, comparing each window's local slope against the near-origin reference window ([0,0.04) rad). Departure stays within +/-15% of the reference out to ~0.03 rad on both axles, then exceeds 10% and STAYS exceeded (not a single noisy crossing) from window leading edge 0.045 rad (front) / 0.035 rad (rear) onward, climbing to full sign reversal by ~0.08-0.09 rad -- the genuine nonlinear/saturation region. Value set at the more conservative (earlier-onset) axle's sustained-departure point, 0.035 rad, rounded down slightly to 0.03 rad for a safety margin against measurement noise; both axles' own curves are still flat (within a few % of the reference) at 0.03 rad.
stability_estimation._comment_grid_rate: 100 Hz time-base work package (2026-09-02, thesis_notes.md 'PHASE 0: 100 Hz time base'). SUPERSEDES the prior single-value expected_sample_rate_hz exact-match guard (2026-08-31, GT3 Paul Ricard investigation) with an ADAPTIVE grid: target_sample_rate_hz (100) is the PREFERRED base grid -- diagnostics/inspect_native_channel_rates.py found this car's own fast CS-chain channels (sclu_yaw_rate, log_asteer, log_acc_y, log_acc_z, lap_distance) are natively 100 Hz on Dubai, only ecu_speed is natively 50 Hz. prepare_vehicle_state now builds the common time grid at min(target_sample_rate_hz, the slowest of those fast channels' own native rate) -- ecu_speed itself is upsampled onto that grid via the same np.interp already used for every other channel: justified because vehicle speed is an INERTIA-LIMITED signal (cannot jump between real samples), so linear interpolation between genuine 50 Hz speed readings invents no meaningfully wrong information, unlike upsampling a fast-changing quantity like yaw rate would. min_sample_rate_hz (50) is the HARD FLOOR below the target: a file whose fast channels cap BELOW 50 Hz (e.g. the 20 Hz GT3 Paul Ricard export) is still refused outright, naming the binding (slowest) channel -- the guard from 2026-08-31 is not gone, only widened into a range. A file capping exactly AT 50 Hz (e.g. every fast channel measured 50 Hz) processes normally at a 50 Hz grid, no refusal, no degradation beyond one status line (state['grid_rate_status']: 'channel-limited' vs the target). RESIDUAL LEGACY, documented not fixed (thesis_notes.md): tyre_model_ekf.pass_1's frozen R (R_yaw_rate_var/R_ay_var) was calibrated against this car's own PRIOR fixed 50 Hz grid -- carried forward unchanged for a file now running at 100 Hz, a stated limitation of that specific frozen curve, not something this package re-derives. Every OTHER estimator window in this pipeline was already converted to a PHYSICAL-duration/distance basis before or during this same package (cs_min_window_s, yaw_stability_* via window_s/window_m/grid_step_m, longitudinal_stiffness's own regression_window_s) and therefore derives correctly at either grid rate -- EXCEPT kerb_dilation_samples, nis_gate/tyre_fit_auto/tyre_model_ekf's own nis_window_samples, and apex_half_window_samples, which remain literal sample counts NOT rate-corrected by this package (out of its stated scope) -- each now silently represents HALF its originally-calibrated physical duration on a file running at the new 100 Hz grid instead of the old fixed 50 Hz. Flagged, not fixed, same treatment as the pass_1 R note above.

stability_estimation._comment_vertical_load_source: Fz-integration work package, Phase 1 (2026-09-03, branch fz-integration). DEFAULT 'static' = estimate_vertical_loads's own existing chair-parity static/aero/transfer model, completely unchanged -- every session before this package, and every session with no damper data, behaves byte-identically. stability_estimation._comment_gps_course_anchor: WP5b(c), estimate_sideslip_gps (validation-only, no pipeline call site). Drift-correction anchor gate: a sample qualifies once a short-window-smoothed |ay| stays below max_ay_g for a contiguous run of at least min_duration_s. Data-derived on Dubai (diagnostics/inspect_beta_gps_validation.py): raw per-sample |ay| is too noisy for a literal unbroken-run test (2267 candidate runs at the chosen threshold, longest ~0.1s) -- smooth_window_s=0.3 first was necessary to get physically-sized runs (6 runs >=1.5s, 20.4s total anchor time across 4 laps). max_ay_g=0.05 sits at the moving-sample |ay| p10 (0.044g), a natural low-|ay| population before the distribution rises steeply toward cornering values (p20=0.109g).
stability_estimation.gps_course_latency_s_derived_from: diagnostics/inspect_beta_gps_validation.py, WP5b(c) iteration 1 Section 0: cross-correlation of wrap-safe d(course)/dt against -yaw_rate_radps over lags -1..+1s (racing laps, moving samples) peaks at r=0.9898 at lag=+0.32s, vs r=0.9575 at zero lag -- course-derived rotation consistently lags yaw_rate by this much. A stale course reading recorded at time t describes the vehicle's true state at (t - latency); querying it at (t + latency) recovers the value that actually corresponds to the query instant.
stability_estimation._comment_cs_apex_region: CS validity repair part A, Phase 3 (2026-09-02, thesis_notes.md 'apex_3 structural finding'). apex_3 is a single time-instant expanded to a FIXED +/- apex_half_window_samples window (11 raw samples), independent of corner/lap/estimator -- structurally unable to clear the re-derived cs_min_window_samples floor above on its own terms. cs_apex_region_half_length_m defines a DISTANCE-based (not sample-count) span around the apex position for a separate apex_region CS statistic (summarise_corners), consumed by _classify_corner/_phase_verdict wherever an apex_3-keyed CS read is needed, instead of apex_3's own 11-sample slice -- apex_3 itself is unchanged for display and non-CS stats. stability_estimation._comment_yaw_stability: Module 5 estimator (modules/yaw_stability.py), after the chair performance_analysis tooling (internal). stability_estimation._comment_cs_fallback: Fallback cornering stiffness references. Derived from axle normal load × C_alpha/Fz = 12 rad^-1 (Milliken & Milliken, RCVD, GT3 slick). Front: (290+290)*9.81*12 = 68268. Rear: (395+381)*9.81*12 = 91343. Used as C_linear_ref when OLS cannot resolve the linear stiffness from data (insufficient alpha excitation on rear axle). Accuracy Level 1. pass_1.R_ay_derivation: SUPERSEDED by r_q_sweep_note below, history kept for the record. Original single-shot derivation (Method A, fit-residual-based, non-circular): WP-N1b per-axle Dugoff fit RMS residuals (front 2752.7 N, rear 5793.2 N over the SAME base_mask population, n=24183) converted to acceleration (front 2.030, rear 4.272 m/s^2). Independence was checked, not assumed: correlation(resid_front, resid_rear) = 0.8999 (materially correlated) -- combined via the correlated formula, giving combined std=6.1516 m/s^2 (R_ay_var=37.8418), vs 4.7197 m/s^2 (R_ay_var=22.2757) under the independence assumption that was checked and rejected. Method B (direct empirical innovation from an actual pass-0 run, std=1.864 m/s^2, R_ay_var=3.475) was measured too but NOT used as the original derivation -- it is contaminated by pass_0's own wrong R distorting the state trajectory; demoted to a post-hoc convergence check instead. That first-derivation value (R_ay_var=37.8418) was RUN and found to over-correct the ay channel (0.04% NIS exceedance, Kalman gain's ay column collapsed ~180x vs pass_0) -- see r_q_sweep_note for the resolution.
pass_1.R_yaw_rate_derivation: SUPERSEDED by r_q_sweep_note below, history kept for the record. Original derivation, sequenced after R_ay (not simultaneously, to avoid conflating yaw-rate's own model error with a knock-on effect of the ay miscalibration corrupting the shared 2-state update): yaw-rate innovation std was 3.1709 deg/s at pass_0 (R_ay still wrong); after fixing R_ay alone (interim run, R_yaw_rate/Q still at pass_0 values) it dropped to 2.2278 deg/s -- confirming part of the original inflation WAS a knock-on effect, but a substantial independent residual remained. That first-derivation value (R_yaw_rate_var=0.001511889) was RUN and found to under-correct (30.1% NIS exceedance, above the 15% gate) -- see r_q_sweep_note for the resolution.
pass_1.r_q_sweep_note: The two single-shot derivations above landed the two channels on OPPOSITE sides of the 3%-15% NIS-exceedance gate (ay too low at 0.04%, yaw rate too high at 30.1%) -- a scalar rescale of R as a whole cannot fix an imbalance between its own two diagonal entries, so a 2-D grid over (R_ay_scale, R_yaw_rate_scale), each independently multiplying this pass's own first-derivation values, was run instead of restarting from scratch (diagnostics/inspect_ekf_pass1_rQ_sweep.py, Q held fixed -- nothing diagnosed so far implicates Q specifically). Of 25 grid points (R_ay_scale in [1,0.3,0.1,0.03,0.01], R_yaw_scale in [1,2,4,8,16]), exactly one landed both channels inside [3%,15%]: R_ay_scale=0.1 (R_ay_var=3.78418, yaw_exceed=10.0%), R_yaw_scale=4.0 (R_yaw_rate_var=0.0060476, ay_exceed=9.2%) -- the values now stored above. Notable cross-check: R_ay_scale=0.1 lands within 9% of Method B's earlier-demoted empirical estimate (R_ay_var=3.475) -- the contamination concern that demoted Method B was real in principle but turned out not to be a large practical distortion for this specific number.

longitudinal_stiffness._comment: PLAN.md STEP 3 (LS_ratio), additive-only namespace. Phase 1: axle Fx (modules/longitudinal_forces.py) and per-axle slip ratio kappa. Phase 2: the dFx/dkappa windowed-regression estimator (modules/longitudinal_stiffness.py), mirroring the chair performance_analysis tooling's own estimate_longitudinal_stiffness (docs/literature/longitudinal_stiffness_estimator.py, internal) -- cutoff_hz/regression_window_s/min_slip_span/linear_slip_threshold/min_speed_mps below are that module's own LongitudinalStiffnessConfig dataclass defaults, read live from config here instead of hardcoded, per the chair citation's own values (not re-derived for this car -- changing any re-triggers threshold re-derivation per CLAUDE.md). min_samples is NOT one of these -- see min_samples_floor's own comment below for the documented 50 Hz deviation, decided 2026-08-30, full record thesis_notes.md.
longitudinal_stiffness.rear_rolling_radius_offset_derived_from: WP-S1 (thesis_notes.md 'Wheel-speed source characterization (WP-S1)', 2026-08-18): rear axle (log_speed_rl/rr) reads a CONSTANT +1.41% high vs ecu_speed on straight-line samples, throttle-independent (median +1.44% on-throttle vs +1.41% overall) -- diagnosed as a rolling-radius difference, not traction slip. Corroborated independently by WP5b(d)'s GPS-speed k=1.01211 finding (same direction, unrelated measurement chain).
longitudinal_stiffness.drag_coeff_note: NOT sourced, placeholder -- same convention as vehicle.aero.lift_coeff. Inert regardless of this value while vehicle.aero.cross_track_area_m2 stays 0.0 (also not sourced); the fallback Fx tier's drag term evaluates to exactly zero, a documented underestimate, not a sign error.
longitudinal_stiffness.rolling_resistance_coeff_note: NOT sourced, placeholder. Unlike cog_height_m/track_width_m (which cannot legitimately be zero for a real car), zero rolling resistance is a defensible first-order racing-speed approximation on its own (rolling resistance is one to two orders of magnitude below aero drag and traction/braking forces at racing speed for a slick tyre) -- not an invented Tier A magnitude, a documented simplification, same epistemic move as lift_coeff=0.0.
longitudinal_stiffness.brake_front_fraction_fallback_note: Chair performance_analysis tooling's own default_brake_front_fraction constant (docs/literature/longitudinal_stiffness_estimator.py calculate_longitudinal_axle_forces, internal) -- adopted verbatim, used only when log_pbrake_f/log_pbrake_r are both unavailable/invalid (on this session's data both are whitelisted and valid, so the measured-split path is the one actually exercised).
longitudinal_stiffness.min_samples_floor_note: DOCUMENTED DEVIATION from the chair's own min_samples=25 default (decided 2026-08-30, user decision, full record thesis_notes.md 'PLAN.md STEP 3: 50 Hz min_samples adaptation'). FORCING FACT: this car's Cosworth log runs at 50 Hz; the chair's literal min_samples=25 with regression_window_s=0.45 is structurally unsatisfiable at 50 Hz (max window 2*half_window+1 = 23 samples, proven analytically, thesis_notes.md Phase 2 entry) -- LS_ratio was all-NaN under the literal transplant. Adaptation keeps the chair's PHYSICAL window (regression_window_s, unchanged) and derives the actual per-call min_samples in modules/longitudinal_stiffness.py's _centered_slopes at runtime from the ACTUAL sample rate: max(min_samples_floor, half_window+1), so a future higher-rate log auto-scales without re-tuning. This key is the FLOOR only, not the effective value -- at 50 Hz the derived half_window+1=12 is below this floor, so the floor binds (effective min_samples=15 at 50 Hz); the floor exists so an unusually low sample rate cannot validate a near-empty window. Estimator change under the deviation taxonomy (method calibration tunable, was 'match the chair BY CHOICE', now FORCED ADAPTATION) -- re-triggers threshold re-derivation, same rule as any other.
longitudinal_stiffness.plausibility_kappa_bound_note: NEW, additive (decided 2026-08-30, user decision, full record thesis_notes.md 'LS plausibility guard' and its own 'Kerb-strike wheel-speed spikes' investigation entry). Same value as that investigation's gap-selected ANOMALY_THRESHOLD: the non-kerb-masked racing population's own |kappa_wheel| p99.9 (11.444%), rounded up to 12.0% -- everything above it is rarer than 1-in-1000 among samples the kerb mask does not already flag. Tier B, data-derived from this session's own distribution, not a chair value (no chair equivalent exists). Used ONLY in combination with az-coincidence (modules/longitudinal_stiffness.py _apply_plausibility_guard) -- NEVER applied to kappa alone, see that function's own docstring for why.
longitudinal_stiffness.plausibility_az_window_note: NEW, additive (decided 2026-08-30, user decision). Trailing (backward-looking) window, per axle, over which _apply_plausibility_guard checks for a recent kerb-like az disturbance before excluding an implausible-kappa sample. Sized from thesis_notes.md 'Kerb-strike wheel-speed spikes' PART 1b's measured post-kerb-event settle-time distribution (all 57 racing kerb events, not just a sample): rear (rl+rr) settle p50=160ms p75=560ms -- 0.6s sits just above p75, covering most rear ringdown without reaching into the multi-second tail (p90=2.1s, 2 events never settled within 3s); front (fl+fr) settle p50=0ms p90=396ms -- 0.15s is a conservative user-selected value above the near-zero median, ahead of the visible tail. These are user-chosen working values informed by that distribution, not a formulaic percentile pick -- re-derive if the underlying kerb-event population changes materially (new track, different kerb geometry).

wheel_speed_guard._comment: Fz-integration Phase 5 (2026-09-03), Tier B (signal/data engineering -- a plausibility gate, no vehicle-dynamics method content). modules.longitudinal_forces._guarded_wheel_speed_kmh: per-window (window_s), a log_speed_{corner} window is invalid when EITHER its own std stays below std_min_kmh while the car is moving (stuck) OR its mean ratio to its axle-mate deviates from 1.0 by more than ratio_max_deviation (dropout/spike) -- falls back to abs_speed_{corner} (unit-normalised) where available, NaN otherwise. Motivated by a real, found bug: GT3_PRC_MLA-v3.txt's log_speed_rr reads a spurious 300.5 kph peak (vs its own mates' ~250 kph max) and deviates from log_speed_rl by >15% on 5.9% of moving samples -- diagnostics/inspect_v3_wheel_speed_census.py, thesis_notes.md 'Fz-integration Phase 5...'. Consumers: modules.longitudinal_forces.estimate_slip_ratio (kappa_f/kappa_r) and, through it, modules.longitudinal_stiffness's own kerb-adjacent plausibility guard -- both read the guarded channel automatically, no separate wiring.
wheel_speed_guard.window_s_note: Physical window duration, rate-derived to samples at runtime (same pattern as stability_estimation.cs_min_window_s) -- not independently re-derived this session, chosen as a plausible sub-second fault-detection window matching this project's other window-based guards (NIS gate 0.4s, kerb az windows 0.15-0.6s).
wheel_speed_guard.std_min_kmh_note: Stuck-while-moving floor. FIRST VALUE TRIED (1.0 kph) WAS WRONG, caught empirically before shipping (diagnostics/inspect_wheel_speed_guard_before_after.py's own first run flagged 22-45% of samples on every corner of BOTH sessions, including Dubai's known-healthy channels -- traced to this threshold, not the ratio check, which independently measured only 0.19% false-positive on the same Dubai FL/FR pair): a 0.5s window's real, healthy std is itself often below 1.6 kph (Dubai log_speed_fl, moving windows: p10=0.53, p25=0.91, p50=1.61 kph) -- 1.0 kph sat in the middle of NORMAL variation, not below it. 0.1 kph sits ~5x below that real p10, a genuine margin above true zero-variance rather than a guess -- the ratio-to-mate check is what actually catches real faults (v3's log_speed_rr, thesis_notes.md 'Fz-integration Phase 5...'); this stuck check is a rarely-firing defensive second condition, evaluated only on moving samples so genuine standstill is never mistaken for a stuck sensor.
wheel_speed_guard.ratio_max_deviation_derived_from: Gap-selected against v3's own log_speed_rr/log_speed_rl ratio-deviation distribution (moving samples, diagnostics/inspect_v3_wheel_speed_census.py): the real/plausible population sits below its own p90 (4.62% deviation -- ordinary cross-axle cornering differential and sensor noise), the fault population's own p95 is already 20.40% -- 10% sits in the gap between the two, well clear of both.
wheel_speed_guard.abs_speed_channel_note: abs_speed_fl/fr/rl/rr (config/channels.json, newly whitelisted this phase) are the ABS-domain wheel-speed alternative -- present and 100Hz on BOTH real sessions (v3 unit 'kph', Dubai unit 'mph', confirmed directly per file, same per-file-unit hazard as log_susp_travel/lap_distance -- modules.longitudinal_forces._normalize_wheel_speed_to_kmh converts, never assumes).

wheel_loads._comment: Damper/suspension-travel-derived per-wheel vertical load (Fz), additive-only namespace. Method anchor: thesis_notes.md wheel-load entry (Segers, Analysis Techniques for Racecar Data Acquisition, ch.9 p.199 / ch.10 pp.221-256 -- page anchors to verify against the docs/literature copy). Channels first available on GT3_PRC_MLA-v3.txt (thesis_notes.md 'GT3_PRC_MLA-v3 census'), whitelisted in config/channels.json. Registers as a Level 4 source (modules/wheel_loads.py) per corner where log_dms_dam_*/log_susp_travel_* are both valid; static-split (modules.stability_analysis.estimate_vertical_loads, Level 1) remains the fallback per corner, never a whole-session all-or-nothing switch.
wheel_loads.pushrod_offset_note: Level 1 default (zero). 'Pushrod gauges give absolute force via entered offsets' per the work order -- log_dms_dam_* is already logged in [N] (confirmed from the raw file header, not assumed), so an offset here is a zero-load calibration correction the team would enter after a static gauge check, not a unit conversion. No such session-entered value exists yet anywhere in this project (no UI field, no setup_data key) -- left at 0.0 (i.e. the raw channel is trusted as already zeroed) until a real calibration procedure and entry point exist. Phase 2's straight-line total-load validation is the check on whether 0.0 is a reasonable assumption for this file.
wheel_loads.unsprung_mass_note: Level 1, work-order-supplied figures (not independently sourced this package) -- per-wheel unsprung mass (upright, hub, brake, wheel/tyre assembly, half-shaft share), typical order of magnitude for a GT3-class car. Feeds the unsprung-mass lateral-transfer term, which bypasses the damper/spring entirely (reacts through the upright/tyre contact directly) and must be added on top of the damper-derived sprung force, never folded into it.
wheel_loads.tyre_dynamic_radius_note: Level 1 ESTIMATE, not a measured dynamic (loaded) radius. Derived from the team-supplied STATIC tyre circumference (thesis_notes.md 'Rolling circumference: three disagreeing numbers, none resolved', front 2140mm / rear 2210mm, itself flagged TODO-verify, no datasheet seen) via radius = circumference/(2*pi): front 2140/(2*pi)=340.6mm, rear 2210/(2*pi)=351.8mm. Dynamic (loaded, rolling) radius is normally a few percent smaller than static/free radius under load -- this approximation is NOT corrected for that effect. Used only for the unsprung-mass transfer arm h_u; listed here explicitly as an estimate needing a better source, per the work order's own instruction not to invent precision.
wheel_loads.roll_centre_note: Level 1 ESTIMATE. Read from config/car_data.json kinematic_variants_front/rear's own stated baseline_variant (FS15 front, RS25 rear) roll_center_mm column, converted mm->m -- NOT confirmed against which kinematic variant is actually fitted for the GT3_PRC_MLA-v3 session (no setup record identifies it). Used for the sprung-mass GEOMETRIC lateral-transfer term (the portion of roll-induced load transfer carried through the suspension linkage/roll axis rather than through spring compression) -- this is the only sprung-mass transfer component added on top of the damper-derived force; the ELASTIC portion is already present in the measured pushrod force itself and must not be added twice.
wheel_loads.arb_motion_ratio_approximation_note: Work-order-authorised approximation: no dedicated ARB-linkage motion ratio is digitised anywhere in car_data.json (only 'N/mm at drop link' rate tables plus a scalar ratio_to_wheel). modules/wheel_loads.py approximates the ARB's own travel-to-wheel motion ratio with the SAME damper motion_ratio_vs_wheel_travel value used for the pushrod force at that instant (axle-matched) -- an approximation, not a measured ARB kinematic curve, flagged per corner in the module's own docstring.
wheel_loads.arb_position_fallback_note: Level 1 fallback ARB blade position (1-7) used only when no per-corner session setup value (setup_parameters arb_fl/fr/rl/rr) is available for the file being analysed -- GT3_PRC_MLA-v3.txt carries no setup-sheet record. 4 sits inside setup_parameters.json arb_fl's own recorded typical_window (3-5), a reasonable mid-stiffness assumption, not a measurement of this session's actual ARB setting.
wheel_loads.bump_rubber_note: NEGLECTED (documented limitation, not modelled). No bump-rubber engagement detection or force contribution is included in this estimator -- a wheel deep enough into bump to contact its bump rubber will read an UNDER-estimated load (the rubber's own reaction force is invisible to this decomposition, only the main spring/damper and ARB paths are modelled). config/car_data.json's own bump_stop_curve (cellasto_20mm_40shore) exists but is not consumed here; a future upgrade could use log_susp_travel_* proximity to the bump-stop engagement point to flag (not correct) affected samples.
wheel_loads.aero_front_fraction_note: Level 1 PLACEHOLDER, not measured for this car. Front/rear split of modules.wheel_loads.estimate_session_corrected_axle_totals's own session-fitted aero coefficient c_session (a per-session MEASUREMENT, Level 2 -- this split fraction is the only unsourced part of that correction). 0.40 front / 0.60 rear assumes a rear-biased aero balance, typical of GT3-class cars where a large rear wing dominates a comparatively small front splitter's downforce contribution -- a reasonable order-of-magnitude assumption, not a measured value for this specific car. Listed here explicitly, per the work order, for the user/engineer to replace with real aero-balance data (front/rear downforce split from a windtunnel or CFD report) when available; every wheel_loads reconstruction result that used this split states the value in its own returned dict (aero_front_fraction key).
wheel_loads.dead_channel_std_max_travel_mm_derived_f: Fz-integration Phase 1 (2026-09-03): Sample_Dubai.txt's log_susp_travel_rr found frozen (std=0.101mm, range=3.03mm over the whole session) vs its own axle-mate log_susp_travel_rl (std=5.39mm) and every other travel channel checked on both real sessions (Dubai fl/fr/rl: 5.13/6.52/5.39mm; GT3_PRC_MLA-v3 fl/fr/rl/rr: 4.88/7.01/7.20/4.87mm) -- a real dead/disconnected sensor, not a quiet corner (this file's own log_dms_dam_rr force channel is NOT frozen, std=2031N, so the wheel itself is moving, only its travel POT is not). 1.0mm sits with wide margin above the frozen channel (~10x) and well below every real channel's own std (~5x), a gap-selected floor in the same style as this project's other frozen-value guards.
wheel_loads.dead_channel_std_max_force_N_derived_fro: Fz-integration Phase 1 (2026-09-03). No real frozen damper-force example has been observed yet (every log_dms_dam_* channel checked on both real sessions reads std 1489-2083N) -- this floor is set conservatively low (roughly 30-40x below the smallest real std seen) so it cannot false-flag a genuine but quiet corner, pending a real frozen-force case to calibrate against directly the way the travel floor above was. Same guard purpose: a channel logged 'valid' quality and sitting at a plausible constant value is still dead, and channel_quality_gates' own range check cannot see that (it checks the VALUE, not whether it varies).

Not a science/analysis parameter, purely a plotting-window default; clamped at each lap's own s_m extent in ui/views/corner_trace_dialog.py, never fabricates data before/after what that lap actually recorded. corner_trace_display.cs_ls_panel_y_range_note: Cleanup pass, Phase 1: fixed y-range shared by the CS ratio and LS ratio panels in ui/views/corner_trace_dialog.py -- both are the same 1/0/negative scale, but LS_ratio's occasional numerically-unstable windows (see Phase 0's finding) would otherwise force auto-range so wide the meaningful 0..1 region collapses. Data-derived from CS_ratio's own observed range on Dubai at the production kinematic config (min -3.065 rear / -1.872 front, checked 2026-09-01) plus headroom. Display-only clip, out-of-range samples simply not drawn -- pending Phase 0's own open decision on LS_ratio's numerical stability, which may supersede this.
corner_trace_display.ls_display_min_ax_mps2_note: NEW, additive (Cleanup/reliability/presentation pass, Part A item A4, 2026-09-01). Display-only mask: the corner-trace LS panel only draws a sample where |ax_mps2| exceeds this bound -- LS_ratio is a longitudinal-stiffness ratio and reads as noise, not signal, while the car is near-constant-speed (cruise/apex-coast), independent of the Phase 0 numerical-instability finding. Value chosen from this session's own |ax_mps2| distribution over the same base racing population as thesis_notes.md section 13's LS_ratio stats (moving & ~kerb & valid-lap racing time, n=24183): p5=0.474, p10=0.947, p20=1.807, median=3.970 m/s^2 -- this track's laps spend most of their time under real braking/traction demand, so even a modest cutoff excludes only the genuinely flat segments. 1.0 m/s^2 (~0.1g) is the standard vehicle-dynamics rule-of-thumb for negligible longitudinal load transfer, sits just above the p10 point of this distribution, and leaves the great majority (89.4%) of racing-time samples display-eligible (still subject to LS_ratio's own finite/masking gates on top). Tier C, no estimator/threshold change -- LS_ratio's own numeric output is untouched, only what the corner-trace panel draws.
corner_trace_display.default_laps_shown_note: NEW, additive (trace-dialog addendum item 2, 2026-09-01). Corner trace default: when opened from an 'All laps' analysis (a single-lap analysis still defaults to just that lap, unchanged), the fastest N valid laps of this corner start CHECKED, the rest start unchecked but available -- avoids a wall of overlapping colours on a corner with many laps by default while never refusing to show more if the user checks them. N=5 chosen as a readable default under the addendum's own 10-colour palette (comfortably below the point where the dash-cycling fallback would ever trigger). Tier C UI default, not a science/analysis parameter.

accuracy_levels._comment: Single source of truth for per-quantity accuracy (1=config default, 2=session measurement, 3=logged sensor, 4=lookup table; upgrade each node independently, CLAUDE.md/thesis_notes.md). Each node: level (current STATIC/default tier, what a run with no session data resolves to), source (what currently provides the value), capped_by (why it isn't higher: 'chained-constant: <name>' when a Level-1 config constant sits in the node's own derivation chain, 'provenance-assumption: <name>' when no such constant exists but a documented, unverifiable assumption about the channel's own measurement caps it anyway, or null when neither mechanism applies). Consolidated 2026-07-26 -- see thesis_notes.md for the yaw_rate=3 vs steering_angle=1 resolution evidence. WP-C (2026-07-26) adds per-session dynamic resolution on top of this static registry, in modules/accuracy_resolution.py: leaf nodes (mass, corner_weights, and in future WPs steering_ratio/speed/sideslip_angle) carry a real ordered source list there and resolve independently per outing; derived nodes have no source list of their own and instead cascade from the nodes named in capped_by -- either a PURE cascade (resolved level = input's resolved level exactly, e.g. cog_position from corner_weights) or a METHOD-CEILINGED cascade bounded by an explicit method_ceiling field below (the derivation is itself an approximation whose error a better-measured input cannot shrink, e.g. yaw_inertia's m*a*b formula). Every node not dynamically wired yet stays single-source at its level below regardless of any global cap, until its own future WP gives it a second source.

wheel_load_damper.note: Damper package Phase 1 (2026-09-02). Per-CORNER, not per-session: a corner whose damper or travel channel is missing/failed (e.g. GT3_PRC_MLA-v3.txt's own faulted log_dms_dam_fr) falls back to per_wheel_load_split's Level 1 static estimate for that corner alone, recorded per-sample, never a silent session-wide substitution. Not yet wired into modules/accuracy_resolution.py's dynamic per-session cascade or any UI/pipeline consumer -- same incremental scope as per_wheel_load_split's own phase 1 entry above (estimator + static registry first, consumer wiring deferred).

wheel_load_damper_reconstructed.source: quasi-static heave/pitch axle-total (vertical_load_split's own fz_f_N/fz_r_N) minus the real damper-measured axle-mate (modules/wheel_loads.py reconstruct_missing_corner), used ONLY where exactly one corner of an axle is damper-invalid and its mate is damper-valid -- Segers modal-decomposition method, thesis_notes.md 'FR reconstruction: quasi-static modal decomposition' entry
wheel_load_damper_reconstructed.capped_by: chained-constant: vertical_load_split (cog_height_m, aero lift_coeff/cross_track_area_m2/diff_cog_x_m -- the axle-total half of this method), wheel_load_damper (the measured-mate half)
wheel_load_damper_reconstructed.note: Morning follow-up, damper package Item 2 (2026-09-03). Deliberately registered at the SAME nominal Level 1 as per_wheel_load_split despite using three real sensors -- the accuracy-level system records provenance TIER (what kind of source), not within-tier confidence, and this method's own axle-total term is capped by the same unsourced Level-1 aero/cog-height placeholders per_wheel_load_split already carries. In practice more accurate than a pure static-split guess for the missing corner (it uses a real measurement for 3 of the 4 unknowns instead of 0), but that is a within-Level-1 distinction this registry does not represent numerically. Cascade position: tried AFTER wheel_load_damper (Level 4, that corner's own sensor), BEFORE per_wheel_load_split (Level 1 static-only fallback) -- modules.wheel_loads.combine_with_reconstruction_and_fallback implements the three-tier order. LIMITATIONS (full detail in reconstruct_missing_corner's own docstring and thesis_notes.md): a single-wheel event unique to the reconstructed corner is invisible (the axle-total model has no road-input sensing); the warp/torsion mode ((FL+RR)-(FR+RL)) is unobservable with three sensors and a heave/pitch-only model; both corners of the same axle invalid at once falls through to per_wheel_load_split instead (no reconstruction possible from one equation with two unknowns).
